title: Working with GPUs
intro: GPUs are the most expensive resource in most ML platforms. Knowing whether they're actually being used — and whether your workload can even see them — saves real money and debugging time.

steps.prompt: Check the GPUs on this training machine: utilization, memory, and which processes are using them.
steps.fake_output:
| GPU  Name        | Memory-Usage        | GPU-Util |
|  0   A100-SXM4   | 38012MiB / 40960MiB |   23%    |
| Processes: PID 4821  python train.py  38000MiB |
steps.explanation: Memory is nearly full, but compute utilization is only 23%.
steps.why: Full memory with low utilization is a classic sign the GPU is waiting on something else — usually the data loader. The fix is often more DataLoader workers or faster storage, not a bigger GPU.

steps.prompt: Watch GPU usage refresh every second while training runs.
steps.explanation: Utilization swings between near-full and nearly idle.
steps.why: That sawtooth pattern confirms the input pipeline is the bottleneck: the GPU finishes each batch, then idles while the next one loads. Averaged metrics hide this; watching it live makes it obvious.

steps.prompt: Get just utilization and memory as CSV, for logging or scripting.
steps.explanation: Machine-readable output with just the fields you asked for.
steps.why: This is how you'd feed GPU stats into a monitoring system if the NVIDIA DCGM exporter isn't available — dcgm-exporter plus Prometheus is the standard production approach.

steps.prompt: Check how many GPUs each Kubernetes node advertises to the scheduler.
steps.explanation: Two nodes have 8 GPUs each; the others have none (null).
steps.why: Pods request GPUs via 'resources.limits: nvidia.com/gpu: 1'. If a GPU node shows null here, the NVIDIA device plugin isn't running on it, and no pod can ever be scheduled onto its GPUs.

steps.prompt: Check how many GPUs on gpu-node-1 are already allocated to pods.
steps.fake_output:
Capacity:
  nvidia.com/gpu:  8
Allocatable:
  nvidia.com/gpu:  8
Allocated resources:
  nvidia.com/gpu   8   8
steps.explanation: All 8 GPUs are allocated — a new GPU pod will stay Pending until one frees up.
steps.why: GPUs aren't shared between pods by default — a pod holding a GPU holds all of it, even if idle. Idle notebooks and finished-but-not-deleted jobs silently hoarding GPUs is extremely common (see mlops-incident-003).
